name: Kaynes Technology India Ltd
about: Incorporated in 2008, Kaynes Technology is a leading end-to-end and IoT solutions-enabled integrated electronics manufacturing company. The company provides conceptual design, process engineering, integrated manufacturing, and life-cycle support for major players in the automotive, industrial, aerospace and defense, outer-space, nuclear, medical, railways, Internet of Things ("IoT"), Information Technology ("IT") and other segments. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 53.9% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 105.2%.
EBITDA margin expanded 590 bps over 5 years (10.0% → 15.9%).
Revenue growth slowed from 22% to 4% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 12.6%, 350 bps below a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹977 cr of profit, −₹615 cr of operating cash — conversion -0.63x — profits are not turning into cash.

flags.text: Profits not turning into cash: 5-yr CFO/PAT -0.63x
Large capex underway: CWIP ₹706 cr = 34% of fixed assets

ledger.quote: by end of the financial year we'll turn the cash positive
ledger.statement: Cash-positive (operating cash flow) by end of FY27
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: The same promise was made for FY26 (G15) and rolled forward. Q1 FY27 showed about INR 259 crore of negative cash flow from inventory (+INR 177 crore) and receivables (C3); Q2 FY27 PAT fell 65.5% YoY; cash conversion cycle is 193 days vs 162 three years ago; 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63. Getting to positive FY27 OCF needs a large H2 working-capital release that the inputs do not show yet.
ledger.actual_text: Q1 FY27 negative cash flow ~INR 259 crore (C3); H1 figure not in inputs

ledger.quote: we are pretty confident that we will be able to do the turnaround by end of this year in terms of receivables from the metering business
ledger.statement: Metering-business receivables turnaround by end of FY27
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: One quarter in, receivables still rose by INR 68-90 crore in Q1 FY27, 'mainly because of metering' (C3), even after management cut metering supply to force collections (C1). Earlier receivable commitments (INR 240 crore discounting, G23; 90-day collection goal, G24) have no confirmed delivery in the inputs.
ledger.actual_text: Q1 FY27 receivables +INR 68-90 crore, mainly metering (C3)

ledger.quote: is about INR300 crores for OSAT, INR300 crores for PCB, and about INR250 crores for EMS business
ledger.statement: FY27 capex of about INR 850 crore: OSAT 300, PCB 300, EMS 250
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Management said 'we are on track' after Q1 FY27 spend of about INR 230 crore (OSAT 90, PCB 90, EMS 50), 27% of the INR 850 crore plan in 25% of the year (C5). Q2 spend is not in the inputs. Management also said modular expansions will continue 'as and when we get the newer business', so the total could rise.

ledger.quote: we have committed a full year revenue of totally INR500 crores between both
ledger.statement: OSAT and PCB full-year FY27 revenue of INR 450-500 crore, starting Q3
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Revenue is guided to start in Q3 FY27, which has not been reported. The FY27 figure (INR 450-500 crore for half a year) is below the INR 550-700 crore combined PCB and OSAT production value cited in Q4 FY26 (G12, G13), though those carried no stated horizon.

ledger.quote: we have committed the 2x of the market growth
ledger.statement: Revenue growth of 2x the market growth (no absolute number given)
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: With the market at 16-18% (G7), 2x implies 32-36% growth. Q1 FY27 delivered 40.6% but Q2 FY27 only 4.5%; H1 FY27 works out to roughly 20% (derived from F:ttm_revenue_cr, FY26 revenue of INR 3,632 crore and the quarterly growth rates). Hitting 32-36% for FY27 would need H2 revenue ~41-48% above H2 FY26. FY26 itself missed plan (G14).
ledger.actual_text: Q2 FY27 revenue +4.5% YoY; H1 FY27 ~20% (derived)

ledger.quote: our goal is to steadily increase the contribution of NPD-led and value-added solutions to nearly 30% of the total revenue in the coming years
ledger.statement: NPD-led and value-added solutions to reach nearly 30% of revenue
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: No current NPD-led/value-added revenue share is disclosed in the inputs and no date was given beyond 'the coming years'.

ledger.quote: we'll double the growth of market growth is what the commitment that we have done
ledger.statement: Revenue growth at twice the EMS market growth (market 16-18%)
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Restated as G5 in Q1 FY27. A 16-18% market implies 32-36% growth; Q2 FY27 revenue growth was 4.5% and H1 FY27 roughly 20% (derived), after Q1's 40.6%.

ledger.quote: So rail business, I'm expecting this year to grow by around 20%, 25%
ledger.statement: Rail business growth of 20-25% in FY27
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: FY27 has not ended. C2 says railways grew in Q1 FY27 but gives no rate, and the company says it does not normally disclose segment numbers (C2), so this may end unverifiable.

ledger.quote: the margins are going to be north of current 30% plus
ledger.statement: Rail margins above 30% in FY27
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: No rail segment margin is in the inputs and the company does not normally disclose segment data (C2). Consolidated margin fell to 12.6% in Q2 FY27 from 16.1% a year earlier, which says nothing direct about rail.

ledger.quote: That is why I have committed that it will take up to the third quarter for us to complete this.
ledger.statement: Complete smart-meter installations by Q3FY27
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: The Q1 FY27 call says installations were hit by floods and that metering was deliberately cut until collections improve (C1); metering revenue fell to INR 210 crore in Q1 (C2). Q3 FY27 has not been reported.
ledger.actual_text: Q1 FY27 metering revenue INR 210 crore (C2)

ledger.quote: For the next year, while the INR971 crores of sales, what we did this year, in absolute numbers, we may remain same or slightly up or down
ledger.statement: Smart-meter sales of about INR971 crore in FY27, roughly flat
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 metering revenue of INR 210 crore (C2) annualises to ~INR 840 crore, 13% below FY26's INR 971 crore, and management says it chose to degrow metering until collections improve (C1). The guide allowed 'slightly up or down', so a shortfall would be by choice rather than lack of orders, but the Q1 run-rate is outside 'roughly flat'.
ledger.actual_text: Q1 FY27 INR 210 crore (~INR 840 crore annualised)

ledger.quote: PCB of around INR300 crores to INR400 crores
ledger.statement: PCB production value of INR300-400 crore
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: PCB revenue is guided to start in Q3 FY27 (G4) and FY27 PCB capex is INR 300 crore (G3); no production value reported yet and no horizon was given.

ledger.quote: OSAT of around INR250 crores to INR300 crores
ledger.statement: OSAT production value of INR250-300 crore
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: OSAT revenue is guided to start in Q3 FY27 (G4) and FY27 OSAT capex is INR 300 crore (G3); no production value reported yet and no horizon was given.

ledger.quote: we'll cross about INR4,000 crores minimum
ledger.statement: FY26 revenue of at least INR 4,000 crore including Q4
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: Check: FY26 revenue INR 3,632 crore, 9.2% below the INR 4,000 crore floor. The 4,000 was already a cut from the INR 4,500 crore guided at the start of the year (C6), so the shortfall to original guidance is 19%. Management blamed a ~90% revenue drop at a single-source EV customer and delayed government orders (C7, C8). Its claim of ~33% FY26 growth (C7) does not reconcile with 4,500 being 'almost 55% growth' (C6), which implies an FY25 base near INR 2,900 crore and ~25% growth at 3,632.

ledger.quote: at consol level, we'll definitely be OCF positive by end of this year
ledger.statement: Consolidated operating cash flow positive by end of FY26
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY26 OCF is not in the inputs, but in Q1 FY27 management re-promised turning cash positive 'by end of the financial year' (G1), i.e. the FY26 deadline passed without it. The Q4 FY26 call said total net working capital rose because of metering (C9); 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63 and 5-year FCF is -INR 3,287 crore.
ledger.actual_text: Not reported in inputs; target rolled to FY27 (G1)

ledger.quote: At a consol level, we'll definitely deliver this number of $1 billion.
ledger.statement: Consolidated revenue of USD 1 billion in FY28, with individual targets possibly higher
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY28 target. No exchange rate is in the inputs, so the gap to TTM revenue of INR 3,946 crore cannot be sized. The base has slipped: FY26 delivered INR 3,632 crore vs INR 4,500 crore originally guided (C6), and Q2 FY27 growth fell to 4.5%.

ledger.quote: maybe about another INR400-odd crores of capex will be spent
ledger.statement: Further capex of about INR 400 crore in the rest of FY26
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: No FY26 capex figure is in the inputs. 5-year FCF of -INR 3,287 crore shows heavy cumulative investment but cannot isolate Q4 FY26 spend.

ledger.quote: we'll spend about cumulatively INR1,400 crores in the PC Board business
ledger.statement: Cumulative PC Board capex of INR 1,400 crore in FY27 (Phase 1 completed)
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY27 PCB capex was reiterated at INR 300 crore with ~INR 90 crore spent in Q1 (C5, G3); cumulative spend to date is not disclosed, so the INR 1,400 crore total (also G22) cannot be tracked yet. PCB revenue is due from Q3 FY27 (G4).

ledger.quote: which will total up to about between INR700 crores and INR800 crores of smart metering business for the year
ledger.statement: Smart metering revenue of INR 700-800 crore in FY26
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: The Q4 FY26 call gives FY26 metering sales of INR 971 crore (G11), 21% above the top of the 700-800 range. The overshoot came in the business carrying most receivables (C9: metering ~25% of revenue but ~67% of receivables, transcript garbled) and preceded the FY26 OCF miss (G15) and the Q1 FY27 decision to cut metering (C1).

ledger.quote: we are not going to implement any more capex in the EMS business
ledger.statement: No EMS capex beyond committed numbers; only debottlenecking spend
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: The Q1 FY27 plan still includes INR 250 crore of EMS capex for FY27 (G3, C5), and management added that 'modular capacity expansions will go on' as new business comes. The inputs do not state the earlier 'committed' EMS number, so whether 250 is within it cannot be judged.
ledger.actual_text: FY27 EMS capex plan INR 250 crore; Q1 spend ~INR 50 crore (C5)

tones.why: Management says it is on target for capex, OSAT and PCB revenue and a cash-positive year-end, and says it has improved on last quarter's commitments, though it declines to give an absolute revenue number.

tones.label: defensive
tones.why: Management acknowledges the missed guidance and apologises ("it is not a denied order, it is a delayed order") while reasserting its targets.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management commits to revenue above INR 4,000 crore, consolidated OCF positivity and USD 1 billion revenue in FY28, while declining to give quarterly guidance because a railway product was postponed.

context.speaker: Muthukumar N.
context.text: Thank you, Mr. Ramesh, and a very good morning to everyone. Thank you all for joining us today early in the morning. Before we take you through the quarter, I want to first address the restatement that you would have seen in the Notes 9 and 10 of the results. In line with the expectation from the wider investing community and with the objective to strengthen the reporting process, we have transitioned to a larger audit firm and have completed our first quarterly limited review with our new auditor, Walker Chandiok & Co LLP. The process followed a detailed review with our prior period numbers with them, and after extensive discussion with the audit committee, the management team felt a restatement under Ind AS 8 was the right way to deal with it. The comparatives of Q1 FY27, Q2 and H1 FY26, and FY26, and the opening balance sheet of 1st April 2025 also have been restated and shown in our filing. At the consolidated level, the FY26 PAT now stands at INR392 crores against the INR364 crores earlier reported, which shows how conservatively the organization has been doing in terms of the profitability. The net worth is marginally higher. A good part of the adjustment and reclassification, including the bank-funded receivable and supplier financing line, which was not shown as a part of the borrowing, are now shown as under the borrowings. The consolidated adjustment impacting the P&L were mainly on account of change in accounting of one of the contracts for the Smart Metering business, followed by some accruals and provision, following a detailed review with the auditing teams. Wherever the adjustment corrected genuine errors, we have tightened our control, and I will take you through those. I just wanted to restate the entire reclassification were done due to the interpretat

context.speaker: Muthukumar N.
context.text: Thank you, Mr. Sinha, for giving this. In terms of receivable, if you see in the past, whatever the bill discounting that we are doing for receivables were shown in a separate line item as bill discounting that we have done. Currently, we have restated as a part of the borrowing. This was part of our presentation earlier in investor presentation, and today it has been moved to the borrowing. That is the reason why it is showing that our loans as the thing going up. Second thing, in terms of OSAT and PCB business, specifically the Vishay business is going to come from the existing capacity that we have created. That doesn't mean that we are going to drop the existing customer that we have. 75% to 90% of the capacities will go to the Vishay, and the rest of the capacities will continue to serve our customer whom we are committed. We are going to be very fair, and we thank our partner for accepting this, and we are going to support them also. Hope this clarifies the question.

context.speaker: Muthukumar N.
context.text: It's not that commitment is coming down. We started working with some customers for getting the capacity, and we said we can commit up to this number. Whatever the validation had been done is what we have agreed now, and we are going to keep about 10% to 25% for those customers. However, the faster rate of what is going to come from Vishay is taking the customer to 75%. We'll be focusing on validating this product and applicating this so that the speed to go to market will be much faster. I think that is why we have taken the strategic initiatives, and we will ensure that if the other customers want this, we'll expand it more than what we have planned and make sure that we serve those customers also, while validation will continue to happen.

At the same time, I am pleased to share that a couple of players have shown serious interest in our business, and we are at advanced stage of closing the deal with partner that is most beneficial for Kaynes, both financially and strategically. We had committed earlier by the February investor call, we will give a proposal on how we are going to do that. I just wanted to reconfirm to you that we are on track for this, and by next quarter end, please, next quarter investor call, please be rest assured that we will come out with a plan. At the same time, our team has worked on several cost improvements in the Smart Meter business.

It's not a denied, it's going to be delayed. Maybe couple of quarters we'll get delayed, but we are there on our target for Mission 30 to achieve the numbers. Thank you, and if you have any other question, please do ask.

Though our inventory levels in terms of the working capital has gone up by about INR150 crores, as I said, this is a strategic decision that we took in the month of February, looking at the global market situation and the volatility. Just because our team has added upon the inventory there, we could able to successfully grow at 40% of plus as an overall, and EMS business alone about 48%. This has -- this inventory increase has helped us, and this will also take us to the next level. We also talked to you earlier about some delayed delivery for a government product.

Sir, we have communicated and we are standing by that. We said we will be funding for this capex for this year is about INR300 crores for OSAT, INR300 crores for PCB, and about INR250 crores for EMS business. We are on track for that. The first quarter spent is about INR90 plus INR90, INR180 plus INR50, INR230 crores, all put together. But we also said that, fund is not a problem, and as and when we get the newer business, the modular capacity expansions will go on. So, and also as and when the subsidies coming, it will keep flowing into the system. This is just to keep a tight control on the cash flows.

Thank you very much for asking this question. We fully understand and appreciate your question. We did an aggressive top line growth in the year based on the order book and we got the electrification of the vehicle. And of course, the government projects where we are working is going to be at the faster pace. Giving a guidance of INR4,500 crores is almost 55% growth over the previous year. In the third quarter, I think we have turned out to saying about INR4,000 crores because of a few delays.

And one of the largest electric vehicle OEM manufacturers has completely dropped by about 90% of the revenue, wherein we were the single supplier which has dropped our numbers. But we were quite confident in the last quarter of getting 2 government orders where the products have been done and the product testing have been approved. It is going to be done, but there is a delayed project. I think these are the 2 things that while we have delivered about 33% growth in revenue and 39% growth in the bottom line, we sincerely understand and appreciate that the guidance what we have given, we could not meet.

business.what_it_does: Electronics manufacturing services (EMS) for railways, automotive (including a large two-wheeler EV maker now in serial production), aerospace and defence, plus a smart-metering business that supplies and installs meters under state-government tenders. OSAT (semiconductor assembly/test) and PCB plants are being built, with revenue guided to start in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: EMS (rail, automotive/EV, aerospace, defence)
segments.comment: Q1 FY27: INR 946 crore total less INR 210 crore metering = ~INR 736 crore (C2); grew ~48% YoY in Q1 vs ~40% overall (C4). The Q4 FY26 call put EMS at 65% of revenue (C9). C2 also cites an unexplained 'INR 90 crores', so the split is approximate.

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.comment: INR 210 crore in Q1 FY27 (C2), deliberately cut to prioritise collections (C1). FY26 metering sales INR 971 crore, ~27% of INR 3,632 crore revenue (G11, G14). Carries a disproportionate share of receivables (C9).

segments.name: OSAT and PCB (new)
segments.comment: No revenue yet; INR 450-500 crore guided for FY27 starting Q3 (G4); FY27 capex INR 300 crore each (G3).

The one beat, FY26 metering revenue of INR 971 crore vs 700-800 guided, came in the business that drove the receivables build.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth momentum: 40% growth in Q1 FY27 with EMS ~48%, every segment growing (C2, C4), and a commitment to grow at 2x the market (G7).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The next quarter broke: Q2 FY27 revenue +4.5% YoY, PAT -65.5%, margin 12.6% vs 16.1% a year earlier. H1 FY27 growth works out to roughly 20%, against the 32-36% that 2x a 16-18% market implies.

narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Cash conversion cycle is 193 days vs 162 three years ago; 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63 and 5-year FCF -INR 3,287 crore; borrowings INR 1,986 crore. The FY26 OCF-positive target (G15) was missed and re-issued for FY27 (G1).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Metering was cut deliberately to collect cash first (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The cut is visible: metering revenue INR 210 crore in Q1 FY27 (22% of INR 946 crore) vs INR 971 crore for FY26 (~27% of revenue). But receivables still rose INR 68-90 crore in the quarter, 'mainly because of metering' (C3). No collection benefit in the numbers yet.

narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q1 FY27 spend of ~INR 230 crore is 27% of the plan in the first quarter, in line with it; debt/equity is 0.4.

bull.point: Q1 FY27 showed what EMS can do: revenue +40.6% YoY with EMS ~48% while metering was cut; a large two-wheeler EV customer moved into serial production and aerospace recovered (C2, C4).
Long-run compounding: revenue CAGR 47.7% (3y) / 53.9% (5y), PAT CAGR 56.5% / 105.2%, margin +590 bps over 5 years; FY26 metering revenue of INR 971 crore beat the 700-800 guide (G19).

New revenue lines: OSAT and PCB are guided to add INR 450-500 crore from Q3 FY27 (G4), 11-13% of TTM revenue of INR 3,946 crore, with FY27 capex tracking plan (INR 230 crore of INR 850 crore in Q1, C5) at debt/equity of 0.4.

bear.point: Q2 FY27 earnings fell sharply: revenue +4.5%, PAT -65.5%, margin 12.6% vs 16.1% a year ago, straight after a quarter of 40.6% growth. No Q2 call commentary is in the inputs to explain it.

Cash burn: 5-year FCF -INR 3,287 crore, CFO/PAT -0.63, cash conversion cycle 193 days (162 three years ago), ROCE 13%. The OCF-positive promise was missed for FY26 (G15) and re-issued for FY27 (G1) after a ~INR 259 crore Q1 outflow (C3).

Guidance record: FY26 revenue guide cut from INR 4,500 crore to 4,000 crore and delivered 3,632 (C6, G14), blamed on a ~90% revenue drop at an EV OEM where Kaynes was sole supplier and on delayed government orders (C7, C8), which is concentration risk the guidance did not allow for. The metering installation deadline (G10) is already hit by floods (C1).

questions: What drove Q2 FY27 revenue growth down to 4.5% and PAT down 65.5% after Q1's 40.6%: an EMS slowdown, a further metering cut, or the still-delayed government order? What was the Q2 EMS/metering split?

What was FY26 consolidated operating cash flow against the promise to be OCF-positive by end-FY26 (G15), how many days are metering receivables outstanding against the 90-day goal (G24), and what H2 FY27 inventory and receivable release underpins the FY27 cash-positive target after Q1's ~INR 259 crore outflow?

How much of the INR 450-500 crore OSAT/PCB revenue guided for H2 FY27 (G4) is under signed orders from qualified customers, and why is it below the INR 550-700 crore production value cited in Q4 FY26 (G12, G13)?
